airgapllm Architecture & Threat Model

Source: ARCHITECTURE.md

1. Mission & Design Philosophy

airgapllm is a privacy-first, CRAN-grade R workbench for running local open-weights Large Language Models (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) on sensitive human-subjects data (clinical notes, therapy transcripts, EMA journals, student essays, patient narratives) under IRB, HIPAA, and FERPA governance.

Every architectural decision follows four invariants:

  1. Fail-Closed Network Isolation: Remote endpoints are rejected before any sensitive text is touched. Generated container specifications enforce --network none, read-only root filesystems, dropped Linux capabilities, and pinned image SHA-256 digests.
  2. Pre-Inference De-Identification: Sensitive text passes through a deterministic pure-R PII redaction or keyed HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymization gate prior to prompt construction (unless the researcher explicitly attests "verified_deidentified").
  3. Zero-PII-Leakage Persistence: Checkpoints, privacy reports, audit trails, and IRB protocol outputs are strictly barred from storing raw input text, raw model prompts, or raw PII values. Re-identification vaults are isolated and encrypted at rest (AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA256).
  4. Reproducible, Crash-Resumable Execution: Model weights, container images, schemas, prompt templates, and decoding hyperparameters are hashed and logged into a tamper-evident SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL ledger, while row-level atomic JSONL checkpointing enables seamless crash recovery across large datasets.

2. Explicit Threat & Privacy Model

2.1 Assets Protected

  • Protected Health Information (PHI) / Personally Identifiable Information (PII): Direct identifiers (names, emails, phones, SSNs, dates/DOBs, MRNs/student IDs, IP addresses, street addresses, custom lab dictionaries) in research text corpora.
  • Pseudonymization Vault & Secret Keys: Mapping tables enabling reversible de-identification.
  • Model Integrity & Experimental Reproducibility: Weight binaries (GGUF / safetensors), container images, prompt templates, schemas, and random seeds.
  • Compliance Evidence: Tamper-evident audit logs and pre-flight isolation attestations reviewed by IRBs and data security officers.

2.2 Threat Matrix & Mitigations

Threat ID Threat Scenario Attack Vector / Failure Mode airgapllm Mitigation
T1: Network Exfiltration Sensitive text sent to external APIs or telemetry endpoints Accidental remote URL (api.openai.com), container outbound access, corporate HTTP proxy hijacking localhost requests, Hugging Face Hub telemetry Hard loopback/Unix-socket URL validation (is_loopback_endpoint()) rejecting userinfo tricks, non-loopback IPs, 0.0.0.0, and remote hostnames; httr2 proxy bypass (noproxy = "*"); --network none + HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, OLLAMA_NOHISTORY=1; preflight_isolation_check() gate before inference.
T2: Weight & Image Tampering Silent container tag mutation (:latest) or corrupted/trojanized model weights Pulling mutable Docker tags or unverified GGUF/safetensors files Mandatory pinned sha256:<64-hex> image digests in airgap_container_spec(); streaming SHA-256 file and directory-manifest verification via verify_model_digest(); digests persisted in every audit entry.
T3: Container Breakout / Persistence Compromised inference runtime modifying container filesystem or retaining sensitive prompts on disk Writable rootfs, privileged capabilities, default root execution, uncleaned temp dirs --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges:true, read-only model mounts (:ro), bounded noexec,nosuid /tmp tmpfs, Apptainer --containall --no-home --net --network none.
T4: PII Leakage into Prompts Unredacted names, MRNs, SSNs, or emails sent to model context window (and potentially echoed or memorized in KV cache/logs) Forgetting manual de-identification prior to batch extraction Mandatory pii_policy parameter in airgap_extract() defaulting to "redact" (or "pseudonymize" with HMAC-SHA256 tokens; "verified_deidentified" requires explicit opt-in and is recorded in the audit trail).
T5: PII Leakage into Logs, Reports & Console Sensitive strings captured in audit logs, privacy summaries, checkpoints, or error tracebacks Logging full prompts/responses, printing vault dictionaries, attaching raw strings to error metadata Strict schema allowlist + forbidden-key rejection (airgap_audit_privacy_error) + active PII scanning on audit metadata; privacy reports emit aggregate counts only; print.airgap_pii_vault() masks all mappings; checkpoints omit raw input text and store only input_sha256 and validated typed outputs.
T6: Vault Compromise Re-identification mapping file exposed on shared lab storage Plaintext CSV/JSON mapping file stored next to processed data Separate vault serialization (pii_vault_save()) with AES-256-CBC encryption + HMAC-SHA256 (Encrypt-then-MAC) authentication tag, random 128-bit IV, and 0600 filesystem permissions.
T7: Mid-Batch Crash / Partial Corruption GPU OOM, HPC Slurm walltime preemption, or workstation power loss at row 12,400 of 50,000 Reprocessing hours of completed work or corrupting an entire monolithic output file Append-only atomic per-row JSONL checkpointing (checkpoint_path) with header compatibility verification (schema_digest, prompt_template_hash, pii_policy); automatic recovery/truncation of partial trailing lines on resume; completed rows skipped deterministically.
T8: Malformed / Hallucinated Model Output Local 7B–8B quantized models emit broken JSON, wrong types, or out-of-range enum labels Silent NA coercion or pipeline crash Strict extraction_schema() validator (validate_extraction()) rejecting extra keys, type mismatches, non-nullable nulls, and constraint violations, paired with bounded automatic structured repair retry prompts (build_repair_prompt()).
T9: Post-Hoc Audit Tampering Retrospective editing or deletion of compliance log rows Plaintext log files altered after an incident Cryptographic SHA-256 hash chain (GENESIS -> entry_1 -> entry_2 -> ...) verified end-to-end by audit_log_verify(), detecting field edits, deletions, insertions, or reordering.

2.3 Explicit Out-of-Scope / Trust Boundaries

  • airgapllm assumes the host OS kernel, Docker/Apptainer daemon, and physical workstation/HPC node are trusted and administered under institutional security controls.
  • Pure-R deterministic PII detection combines high-precision pattern matchers, capitalization/title heuristics, and lab-supplied custom dictionaries; because no regex/heuristic system guarantees 100% recall on arbitrary free text, researchers should combine domain custom dictionaries, review pii_privacy_report(), and rely on the air-gapped container as defense-in-depth.

3. Modular Package Architecture

R/
├── airgapllm-package.R   # Package documentation & shared imports
├── utils.R               # Canonical JSON, SHA-256/HMAC helpers, timestamps, error classes
├── container.R           # Pillar 1: airgap_container_spec(), Docker/Compose/Apptainer emitters,
│                         #           verify_model_digest(), is_loopback_endpoint(),
│                         #           preflight_isolation_check()
├── pii.R                 # Pillar 2: pii_config(), pii_detect(), pii_redact(),
│                         #           pii_pseudonymize(), pii_reidentify(),
│                         #           pii_vault_key/save/load(), pii_privacy_report()
├── schema.R              # Pillar 3a: schema_field(), extraction_schema(),
│                         #            as_json_schema(), validate_extraction(),
│                         #            build_repair_prompt()
├── runtime.R             # Pillar 3b: runtime_ollama(), runtime_openai_local(),
│                         #            runtime_mock(), runtime invocation dispatch
├── extract.R             # Pillar 3c: airgap_extract(), atomic JSONL checkpoint manager,
│                         #            result accessors (extraction_manifest, etc.)
├── audit.R               # Pillar 4a: audit_log_append(), audit_log_read(),
│                         #            audit_log_verify(), zero-PII enforcement
└── irb.R                 # Pillar 4b: generate_irb_narrative() (Markdown & Quarto)

Data Flow Pipeline

Raw Data Frame (sensitive text)
        │
        ▼
[1] Pre-Flight Isolation Gate (preflight_isolation_check)
    - Container hardening flags (--network none, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, pinned digest)
    - Model weight SHA-256 verification (verify_model_digest)
    - Strict loopback / unix-socket / mock endpoint check + proxy check
        │ (FAIL => abort before touching text)
        ▼
[2] Pre-Inference Privacy Gate (pii_redact / pii_pseudonymize)
    - Deterministic priority-ordered span detection & overlap resolution
    - Aggregate-only pii_privacy_report()
    - Optional HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymization -> separate encrypted vault (AES-256-CBC + HMAC)
        │ (Only sanitized text proceeds)
        ▼
[3] Resumable Batch Extraction Loop (airgap_extract)
    - Load/verify JSONL checkpoint header & skip completed row IDs
    - For each pending row:
        Prompt Render -> Local Runtime (Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM / Mock)
        -> Strict Schema Validation -> (on error: Structured Repair Retry up to max_retries)
        -> Atomic JSONL Checkpoint Append (no raw text stored)
        │
        ▼
[4] Typed Tibble Assembly + Audit Trail + IRB Protocol
    - Strict R column types (character, integer, numeric, logical, enum)
    - Optional local re-identification of output columns via vault
    - Hash-chained PII-free JSONL entry (audit_log_append / audit_log_verify)
    - Methods / IRB boilerplate generation (generate_irb_narrative)

4. Container Hardening Specification

4.1 Docker CLI (emit_docker_run) & Compose (emit_docker_compose)

All generated specifications enforce: - Network: --network none (default strict airgap; optional internal: true Compose network with 127.0.0.1 loopback binding when host-to-container HTTP is needed). - Filesystem: --read-only, model directory mounted read-only (-v <model_dir>:/models:ro), bounded tmpfs (--tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=512m). - Linux Security: --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges:true, optional non-root --user. - Image Pinning: <image>@sha256:<64-hex> (mutable tags without digest are rejected by preflight). - Offline Telemetry Suppression: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, OLLAMA_NOHISTORY=1, OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:<port>. - GPU Passthrough (Optional): --gpus <devices> (NVIDIA) or --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri (AMD ROCm).

4.2 HPC Apptainer (emit_apptainer_def)

Generates a reproducible .def recipe pinning From: <image>@sha256:..., injecting offline %environment variables, provenance %labels (including spec_digest and model_digest), backend %runscript, and documented runtime invocation flags:

apptainer run --containall --no-home --net --network none [--nv|--rocm] \
  --bind <model_dir>:/models:ro <image>.sif

5. Immutable IRB / HIPAA Audit Log Schema (v1.0)

Stored as newline-delimited JSON (.jsonl), one object per line, sorted keys for canonical hashing:

{
  "container_backend": "ollama",
  "container_image_digest": "sha256:...",
  "container_spec_digest": "sha256:...",
  "decoding_params": {
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "seed": 42,
    "temperature": 0,
    "top_p": 1
  },
  "endpoint_class": "loopback",
  "entry_hash": "sha256:...",
  "event_type": "extraction_run",
  "isolation_status": "PASS",
  "model_digest": "sha256:...",
  "model_name": "llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M",
  "network_mode": "none",
  "os_info": "Darwin 23.x arm64",
  "package_version": "0.1.0",
  "pii_config_digest": "sha256:...",
  "pii_counts": {
    "date": 14,
    "email": 3,
    "mrn_id": 12,
    "person_name": 27
  },
  "pii_policy": "redact",
  "preflight_hash": "sha256:...",
  "prev_hash": "GENESIS",
  "prompt_template_hash": "sha256:...",
  "r_version": "4.6.1",
  "row_counts": {
    "failed": 0,
    "processed": 500,
    "resumed": 0,
    "succeeded": 500,
    "total": 500,
    "total_retries": 4
  },
  "run_id": "run_20261123T150000Z_a1b2c3d4",
  "schema_digest": "sha256:...",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "seq": 1,
  "timestamp": "2026-11-23T15:00:00Z"
}

Cryptographic Chain Rule

  • For seq == 1: prev_hash = "GENESIS".
  • For seq > 1: prev_hash = entry[seq - 1].entry_hash.
  • entry_hash = "sha256:" || SHA256(canonical_json(entry without entry_hash)).
  • Canonical JSON sorts all object keys lexicographically at every nesting depth and serializes with auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null", digits = NA.

Zero-PII Enforcement Rule

  • Any entry containing forbidden raw-content keys (text, raw_text, input, prompt, response, output, vault, matches, pii_values, etc.) or triggering pii_detect() on free-text metadata is immediately rejected with an airgap_audit_privacy_error prior to disk write.
